headline: Merge sorted runs of doubling size
statement: Return the linked list in ascending value order. The reference rearranges existing links using bottom-up merge sort, meeting O(n log n) time and constant auxiliary space. Trainer inputs and outputs represent head as an array of values; the trainer supplies the ListNode class and converts arrays to linked lists.
intuition: Merge neighboring sorted sections of the list. Begin with sections of one node, which are already sorted. After merging, sections of two nodes are sorted; the next pass makes sections of four, then eight, and so on. This sorts by changing links rather than copying values into an array.
approach: For run sizes 1, 2, 4, and so on, split two consecutive runs from the remaining list.
Merge those runs by choosing the smaller front node and connect their merged tail to the next pair.
After the final pass, return the new head.
correctness: At the start of a width pass, every width-sized run is sorted. Merging two adjacent sorted runs produces a sorted run of size at most 2*width and preserves its nodes. Thus each pass doubles the guaranteed sorted run size. Once width reaches n, the entire list is one sorted run.
bruteForce: Insertion sort repeatedly searches the sorted prefix, taking O(n²). Top-down merge sort improves time but uses O(log n) recursion storage.

complexity.explanation: There are logarithmically many passes, each scanning O(n) nodes. Only a fixed number of pointers is retained.

pitfalls: Cut each run before merging, or old links may create cycles.
Runs at the end may be shorter than width.
Return the updated head after merging, not the original first node.
